preamble: Spirantization of the voiceless uvular plosive /q/ to the voiceless uvular fricative [χ] keeps the uvular place and turns full closure into frication. In several Quechua I and Ayacucho varieties the change from Proto-Quechua *q is complete, so ⟨q⟩ stands for /χ/. In Kazakh, /q/ is often realized as [χ] in connected speech before consonants, and the /q/–/χ/ contrast is often neutralized in speech.

examples.note: In Ayacucho ⟨q⟩ represents the uvular fricative /χ/, not the uvular stop of Cusco; adjacent vowels are lowered.
Gallagher (2023) reports that in Ayacucho, Pacaraos and Junín Quechua *q is a voiceless fricative [x] or [χ].
Connected-speech realization before a consonant, from the phrase /məqt̪ə d̪i̯͡e-ɡi̯͡en̪/ 'strong say-PFV'.

sources: Gallagher, G. (2023). The phonetic realization of the plain uvular /q/ in a variety of South Bolivian Quechua. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 53(3), 869-887. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100322000135
McCollum, A. G., & Chen, S. (2021). Kazakh. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 51(2). https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100319000185
